QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_8

question.text: Mr. Arjun Desai, a Cost and Management Accountant (CMA) with 4 years of NPO audit experience, wants to become a Social Impact Assessor. Which of the following statements about his eligibility is correct?

answer.text: CMAs are eligible to become SIAs after completing the NISM certification and SRO empanelment, alongside CAs, CSs, and certain UGC graduates/post-graduates with prescribed development-sector experience
CMAs cannot become SIAs — only CAs are eligible
CMAs can become SIAs only after first qualifying as Chartered Accountants
CMAs must be registered with ICMAI's SRO (not ICAI) to function as SIAs

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.3.3 lists the six eligible categories of Social Impact Assessors: CA, CS, CMA, UGC post-graduates with 3+ years development-sector experience, UGC graduates with 6+ years, and others with suitable accreditation with 6+ years. All six qualify through NISM certification plus empanelment with the SRO under ICAI. The Trap: Option B is flatly wrong — CMAs are listed. Option C invents a CA-first prerequisite that doesn't exist. Option D wrongly asserts ICMAI is the SRO for SIAs; it is ICAI for SIAs regardless of the SIA's own base qualification. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A / X-B (IA) and NISM XV (RA) also have eligibility windows by qualification; XXIII broadens the pool to CS/CMA and even experienced graduates, not just CAs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Before accepting a client, verify your own empanelment category is clearly recorded on the ICAI SIAB register — when two SIAs co-sign an AIR, the SE's filing can be rejected if the category appears inconsistent with the signatory's base qualification letter.
